title: eliminate the parameter from a trigonometric parametrization and identify exactly which part of the curve a restricted i
stem: A particle's position at time t is x(t) = 4cos t and y(t) = 3 sin t for 0 ≤ t ≤ π. Which statement describes the path traced?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The entire ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, traced once
choices.rationale: The elimination is right, since cos²t + sin²t = 1 gives x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, but 0 ≤ t ≤ π is only half a revolution, so only part of the ellipse is traced.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The upper half of the ellipse x²/9 + y²/16 = 1, traced from (3, 0) to (−3, 0)
choices.rationale: This swaps the denominators: x = 4cos t means x² is divided by 16, and y = 3 sin t means y² is divided by 9.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lower half of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, traced from (4, 0) to (−4, 0)
choices.rationale: On 0 < t < π we have sin t > 0, so y = 3 sin t is positive and the path is the upper half, not the lower half.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The upper half of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1, traced from (4, 0) to (−4, 0)
choices.rationale: Correct: cos t = x/4 and sin t = y/3, so x²/16 + y²/9 = 1. At t = 0 the point is (4, 0), at t = π/2 it is (0, 3), at t = π it is (−4, 0), and y = 3 sin t ≥ 0 throughout, so it is the upper half from right to left.

stem: A particle's position at time t is x(t) = 2 sin t and y(t) = 5 cos t for 0 ≤ t ≤ π. Which statement describes the path traced?

choices.rationale: Correct: sin t = x/2 and cos t = y/5 give x²/4 + y²/25 = 1. At t = 0 the point is (0, 5), at t = π/2 it is (2, 0), at t = π it is (0, −5), and x = 2 sin t ≥ 0 throughout.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entire ellipse x²/4 + y²/25 = 1, traced once
choices.rationale: The equation x²/4 + y²/25 = 1 is correct, but the interval 0 ≤ t ≤ π is only half a revolution, so only half of the ellipse is traced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The left half of the ellipse x²/4 + y²/25 = 1, traced from (0, 5) to (0, −5)
choices.rationale: Because sin t ≥ 0 on [0, π], x = 2 sin t is never negative, so the path is on the right side of the y-axis, not the left.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The right half of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/4 = 1, traced from (0, 2) to (0, −2)
choices.rationale: This swaps the denominators: x = 2 sin t gives x²/4 and y = 5 cos t gives y²/25, so the long axis is vertical with endpoints (0, ±5).

title: eliminate the parameter from a trigonometric parametrization and identify exactly which part of the curve a restricted i (variant 2)
stem: A particle's position at time t is x(t) = 3cos t and y(t) = 2 sin t for π ≤ t ≤ 2π. Which statement describes the path traced?

choices.label: B

choices.rationale: At t = π the point is (3cos π, 2 sin π) = (−3, 0), not (3, 0), so the motion starts at the left end and moves to the right.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The entire ellipse x²/9 + y²/4 = 1, traced once
choices.rationale: The ellipse equation is correct, but the interval π ≤ t ≤ 2π is only half a revolution, so only the lower half is traced.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lower half of the ellipse x²/9 + y²/4 = 1, traced from (−3, 0) to (3, 0)
choices.rationale: Correct: x²/9 + y²/4 = cos²t + sin²t = 1. At t = π the point is (−3, 0), at t = 3π/2 it is (0, −2), and at t = 2π it is (3, 0), with y ≤ 0 throughout.

title: eliminate the parameter from a trigonometric parametrization and identify exactly which part of the curve a restricted i (variant 3)

title: decide when a moving particle is at a given point by requiring both coordinate equations to hold at the same time, inclu
stem: A particle moves in the plane with position x(t) = t² − 4 and y(t) = t³ − 4t for −3 ≤ t ≤ 3, with t in seconds. At which times is the particle at the origin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: t = −2 and t = 2
choices.rationale: Correct: x(t) = t² − 4 = 0 gives t = ±2. Then y(2) = 8 − 8 = 0 and y(−2) = −8 + 8 = 0, so the origin is reached at t = −2 and t = 2 (the path crosses itself there). At t = 0 the point is (−4, 0).

choices.label: B
choices.text: t = 2 only
choices.rationale: The equation x(t) = 0 gives t = 2 and also t = −2, and y(−2) = 0 as well, so the particle also reaches the origin at t = −2, which is in the interval.

choices.label: C
choices.text: t = −2, t = 0 and t = 2
choices.rationale: Solving y(t) = 0 alone gives t = 0, but at t = 0 the particle is at (-4, 0), not the origin, so both coordinates must be zero together.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At no time; the first zero of y is t = 0, where x = -4
choices.rationale: At t = 0 the particle is at (-4, 0), but that does not rule out other times; both coordinates are zero at t = ±2.

title: read the center, radius, direction and period of circular motion directly from parametric equations.
stem: A bug walks around a circular track: position x(t) = 2 + 4cos(3t), y(t) = −1 − 4 sin(3t), with t in seconds. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The track has center (2, −1) and radius 4; the bug moves counterclockwise and completes one lap every 2π/3 seconds
choices.rationale: The signs on the sine and cosine terms make the bug move clockwise: just after t = 0 it heads downward from the starting point on the track, as the check shows, so the opposite direction is wrong.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The track has center (2, −1) and radius 4; the bug moves clockwise and completes one lap every 2π/3 seconds
choices.rationale: Correct: The terms 4cos(3t) and −4 sin(3t) satisfy ((x − 2)/4)² + ((y + 1)/4)² = 1, so center (2, −1), radius 4. The period is 2π/3. At t = 0 the bug is at (6, −1), the rightmost point, and y decreases for small t, so the motion is clockwise.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The track has center (2, −1) and radius 4; the bug moves clockwise and completes one lap every 2π seconds
choices.rationale: The period is 2π divided by the coefficient of t inside the trigonometric functions, which is 2π/3, not 2π.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The track has center (−2, 1) and radius 4; the bug moves clockwise and completes one lap every 2π/3 seconds
choices.rationale: The center is read from the constants added to the trigonometric terms, with their signs, so the signs of both coordinates cannot be flipped.

title: test points against an implicit relation and use them to decide whether y is a function of x, without swapping coordinat
stem: Consider the relation x² + 4y² = 20. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The points (1, 4) and (1, −4) both lie on the graph, so y is not a function of x
choices.rationale: These points have the coordinates reversed: substituting x = 1, y = 4 gives 65, not 20.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The points (4, 1) and (4, −1) both lie on the graph, so y is not a function of x
choices.rationale: Correct: Substituting (4, 1) gives 16 + 4 = 20, and (4, −1) gives the same value since y is squared. One input x = 4 then has two outputs, so y is not a function of x. Reversed coordinates (1, 4) give 65 ≠ 20.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The point (4, 1) lies on the graph but (4, −1) does not, so y is a function of x
choices.rationale: Since y appears only as y², replacing y with −1 gives the same value 4, so (4, −1) also lies on the graph.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The points (4, 1) and (4, −1) both lie on the graph, and y is a function of x because the graph is symmetric about the x-axis
choices.rationale: Symmetry about the x-axis is exactly what produces two outputs for one input: x = 4 has y = 1 and y = −1, which breaks the definition of a function.

stem: Consider the relation x² + 2y² = 27. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The points (5, 1) and (5, −1) both lie on the graph, so y is not a function of x
choices.rationale: Correct: Substituting (5, 1) gives 25 + 2 = 27, and (5, −1) gives the same value since y is squared. One input x = 5 then has two outputs, so y is not a function of x. Reversed coordinates (1, 5) give 51 ≠ 27.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The points (1, 5) and (1, −5) both lie on the graph, so y is not a function of x
choices.rationale: These points have the coordinates reversed: substituting x = 1, y = 5 gives 51, not 27.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The point (5, 1) lies on the graph but (5, −1) does not, so y is a function of x
choices.rationale: Since y appears only as y², replacing y with −1 gives the same value 2, so (5, −1) also lies on the graph.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The points (5, 1) and (5, −1) both lie on the graph, and y is a function of x because the graph is symmetric about the x-axis
choices.rationale: Symmetry about the x-axis is exactly what produces two outputs for one input: x = 5 has y = 1 and y = −1, which breaks the definition of a function.

title: complete the square on a general second-degree equation to identify the conic and read off its center and the endpoints
stem: The graph of 9x² + 4y² − 36x + 24y + 36 = 0 is an ellipse. Which gives its center and the endpoints of its major axis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Center (2, −3); the major axis is horizontal with endpoints (−1, −3) and (5, −3)
choices.rationale: Completing the square gives (x − 2)²/4 + (y + 3)²/9 = 1, so the larger denominator 9 is under y and the major axis is vertical, not horizontal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Center (2, −3); the major axis is vertical with endpoints (2, 0) and (2, −6)
choices.rationale: Correct: 9(x² − 4x) + 4(y² + 6y) = −36 gives 9(x − 2)² + 4(y + 3)² = 36, so (x − 2)²/4 + (y + 3)²/9 = 1. Center (2, −3), a = 3 vertical, so endpoints (2, 0) and (2, −6).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Center (−2, 3); the major axis is vertical with endpoints (−2, 6) and (−2, 0)
choices.rationale: The center is found from (x − 2) and (y + 3), so it is (2, −3); the signs of both coordinates were flipped.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Center (2, −3); the major axis is vertical with endpoints (2, 6) and (2, −12)
choices.rationale: The endpoints lie √9 = 3 units from the center, not 9 units; the denominator 9 is a² and must be square-rooted.

title: complete the square on a general second-degree equation to identify the conic and read off its center and the endpoints  (variant 1)
stem: The graph of x² − 4y² + 6x + 16y − 11 = 0 is a hyperbola. Which gives its center and its vertices?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Center (3, −2); vertices (1, −2) and (5, −2)
choices.rationale: Completing the square gives (x + 3)² − 4(y − 2)² = 4, so the center is (−3, 2); the signs of both coordinates were flipped.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Center (−3, 2); vertices (−7, 2) and (1, 2)
choices.rationale: From (x + 3)²/4 − (y − 2)² = 1 the vertices are √4 = 2 units from the center, not 4 units; the denominator 4 is a² and must be square-rooted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Center (−3, 2); vertices (−5, 2) and (−1, 2)
choices.rationale: Correct: x² + 6x − 4(y² − 4y) = 11 gives (x + 3)² − 4(y − 2)² = 4, so (x + 3)²/4 − (y − 2)² = 1. Center (−3, 2), a = 2 horizontal, so vertices (−5, 2) and (−1, 2).

choices.label: D
choices.text: Center (−3, 2); vertices (−3, 3) and (−3, 1)
choices.rationale: The positive squared term is the x term, so the hyperbola opens left and right and the vertices are horizontal from the center, not vertical.

title: complete the square on a general second-degree equation to identify the conic and read off its center and the endpoints  (variant 2)
stem: The graph of 4x² + y² + 16x − 6y + 9 = 0 is an ellipse. Which gives its center and the endpoints of its major axis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Center (−2, 3); the major axis is horizontal with endpoints (−4, 3) and (0, 3)
choices.rationale: These are the endpoints of the minor axis: completing the square gives (x + 2)²/4 + (y − 3)²/16 = 1, and the longer axis follows the larger denominator 16 under y.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Center (−2, 3); the major axis is vertical with endpoints (−2, 7) and (−2, −1)
choices.rationale: Correct: 4(x² + 4x) + (y² − 6y) = −9 gives 4(x + 2)² + (y − 3)² = 16, so (x + 2)²/4 + (y − 3)²/16 = 1. Center (−2, 3), a = 4 vertical, so endpoints (−2, 7) and (−2, −1).

choices.label: C
choices.text: Center (2, −3); the major axis is vertical with endpoints (2, 1) and (2, −7)
choices.rationale: The center comes from (x + 2) and (y − 3), so it is (−2, 3); the signs of both coordinates were flipped.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Center (−2, 3); the major axis is vertical with endpoints (−2, 19) and (−2, −13)
choices.rationale: The endpoints lie √16 = 4 units from the center, not 16; the denominator 16 is a² and must be square-rooted.

title: complete the square on a general second-degree equation to identify the conic and read off its center and the endpoints  (variant 3)
stem: The graph of y² − 6y − 8x + 25 = 0 is a parabola. Which gives its focus?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Completing the square gives (y − 3)² = 8(x − 2), so 4p = 8 and p = 2; the focus is 2 units from the vertex (2, 3), not 8.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: The coefficient of (x − 2) is positive, so the parabola opens to the right and the focus lies to the right of the vertex, not to the left.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: y² − 6y + 9 = 8x − 16 gives (y − 3)² = 8(x − 2). Vertex (2, 3), 4p = 8 so p = 2, opening right, so the focus is (4, 3).

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The squared term is y, so the parabola opens horizontally and the focus is found by moving along the x-direction from the vertex, not the y-direction.

title: choose a parametrization that traces an entire implicitly defined curve, checking the denominators, shifts and parameter
stem: Which parametrization traces the entire curve x²/25 + y²/4 = 1 exactly once?

choices.label: A
choices.text: x = 2cos t, y = 5 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π
choices.rationale: This swaps the semi-axes: with these equations x²/25 + y²/4 = 4cos²t/25 + 25 sin²t/4, which is not equal to 1 for all t.

choices.label: B
choices.text: x = 25cos t, y = 4 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π
choices.rationale: The denominators 25 and 4 are the squares of the semi-axes, so the multipliers should be √25 = 5 and √4 = 2, not 25 and 4.

choices.label: C
choices.text: x = 5cos t, y = 2 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π
choices.rationale: Correct: With x = 5cos t and y = 2 sin t, x²/25 + y²/4 = cos²t + sin²t = 1, and 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π covers one full revolution.

choices.label: D
choices.text: x = 5cos t, y = 2 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ π
choices.rationale: These equations do satisfy the relation, but 0 ≤ t ≤ π traces only the upper half of the ellipse, not the entire curve.

title: choose a parametrization that traces an entire implicitly defined curve, checking the denominators, shifts and parameter (variant 1)
stem: Which parametrization traces the entire curve (x − 1)²/9 + (y + 2)²/16 = 1 exactly once?

choices.label: A
choices.text: x = −1 + 3cos t, y = 2 + 4 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π
choices.rationale: These equations center the ellipse at (−1, 2); the relation is centered at (1, −2), so the shifts must be +1 and −2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: x = 1 + 4cos t, y = −2 + 3 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π
choices.rationale: This swaps the semi-axes: the x-direction has denominator 9, so the multiplier on cos t is 3 and the multiplier on sin t is 4.

choices.label: C
choices.text: x = 1 + 3cos t, y = −2 + 4 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ π
choices.rationale: These equations satisfy the relation, but 0 ≤ t ≤ π traces only the upper half of the ellipse, not the entire curve.

choices.label: D
choices.text: x = 1 + 3cos t, y = −2 + 4 sin t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π
choices.rationale: Correct: ((x − 1)/3)² + ((y + 2)/4)² = cos²t + sin²t = 1, and 0 ≤ t ≤ 2π covers one full revolution.

title: choose a parametrization that traces an entire implicitly defined curve, checking the denominators, shifts and parameter (variant 2)
stem: Which parametrization traces the entire parabola y² = 8x?

choices.label: A
choices.text: x = 4t², y = 2t, for all real t
choices.rationale: Here y² = 4t² but 8x = 32t², so the points do not satisfy y² = 8x.

choices.label: B
choices.text: x = 4t, y = 2t², for all real t
choices.rationale: This swaps the roles of x and y: y² = 4t⁴ while 8x = 32t, so the points do not satisfy y² = 8x.

choices.label: C
choices.text: x = 2t², y = 4t, for t ≥ 0
choices.rationale: These equations satisfy the relation, but t ≥ 0 gives y ≥ 0, so only the upper half of the parabola is traced.

choices.label: D
choices.text: x = 2t², y = 4t, for all real t
choices.rationale: Correct: With x = 2t² and y = 4t, y² = 16t² = 8(2t²) = 8x, and as t ranges over all reals y takes every real value, so the whole parabola is traced.

title: choose a parametrization that traces an entire implicitly defined curve, checking the denominators, shifts and parameter (variant 3)
stem: Which parametrization traces the entire curve x = y² + 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: x = t² + 1, y = t, for all real t
choices.rationale: Correct: With y = t and x = t² + 1, we have x = y² + 1, and y = t takes every real value as t ranges over all reals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: x = t², y = t + 1, for all real t
choices.rationale: The shift is placed on the wrong variable: y² + 1 = (t + 1)² + 1 = t² + 2t + 2, which is not equal to x = t².

choices.label: C
choices.text: x = t + 1, y = t², for all real t
choices.rationale: This swaps the roles of x and y: y² + 1 = t⁴ + 1, which is not equal to x = t + 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: x = t² + 1, y = t, for t ≥ 0
choices.rationale: These equations satisfy the relation, but t ≥ 0 gives y ≥ 0, so only the upper half of the curve is traced.
